title: North Korea's crypto machine: the Bitget heist, the Binance billions and the people who paid
angle: Who took the 387.5 million dollars from Bitget and the 6.3 billion from Binance, where did it go, who is behind it, and who loses when a state runs a crypto theft programme?

brief.topic: The North Korean state as a crypto thief: the September 2026 Bitget heist and the wider laundering chain
brief.why: The desk found the Binance story but never asked who was behind it. North Korea now takes the largest share of everything stolen in crypto hacks (76 per cent of value through April 2026), the money finances the regime, and the victims are ordinary account holders.
brief.region: global (Bitget, Dubai/Luxembourg; Lazarus Group; US Treasury OFAC; FBI IC3; UN Seoul)
brief.hints: Bitget hot and warm wallet transfers of 387.5m USD detected 24/25 September 2026; cold wallets untouched; false transaction data inserted into the approval system; CEO Gracy Chen says IP addresses matched VPN choices of a DPRK-linked group and that Lazarus members had posed as a journalist to get a Zoom interview; TRM Labs: DPRK groups took 577m USD with Drift Protocol and KelpDAO and 76 per cent of all 2026 hack value through April; FBI attributed the 1.5bn USD Bybit theft to DPRK in February 2025; DPRK stole 2.02bn USD in 2025, all-time 6.75bn USD; user protection fund above 464m USD; UN Human Rights Office in Seoul and US Treasury OFAC run the counter-measures.

sources.title: Bitget Hack Update: Why Loss Estimate Rise to $387.5M?
sources.text:
Bitget Hack Update: Why Loss Estimate Rise to $387.5M? Bitget Hack Update: When Will Withdrawals Resume After $387M Hit? Sakshi Jain Published: September 26, 2026 Last Updated: 26 Sep 2026 Share: TWITTER Linkedin FACEBOOK Bitget Hack Update 2026: What Happened? When Will Withdrawals Restart? Bitget Exchange found and fixed the bug behind its September 24 crypto hack . The exchange will bring back withdrawals in steps, starting September 28. Bitget also raised its loss estimate to about $387.5 million. The old number was $351.6 million. The new number counts Zcash and TRON assets that were missed at first. At a Glance The exchange spotted the hack on September 24, 2026
Withdrawals restart in steps from September 28
Mandiant and SlowMist are helping with the probe
Bitget started a bounty to help recover funds
Bitget Hack Update: Fixes Vulnerability After September 24 Security Incident
Bitget's security incident team caught bad transfers from a few hot wallets on September 24. This happened at about 18:31 UTC. The team acted fast. It turned on its emergency plan and began digging in. Most of the funds stayed safe. Cold wallets were not touched.
Since then, the team has found how the breach happened. They found the exact bug the attackers used. The bug is now fixed. The exchange also says the exploit is over. No more funds can be taken. Bitget exchange has not shared every detail yet. It says the probe is still open.
At first, it was about $351.6 million that was hit. New checks raised that number to $387.5 million. This does not mean a new hack took place. The higher number just adds in assets on two chains: Zcash and TRON. Those were missed the first time.
The hack touched many chains. This includes Ethereum and other EVM chains, plus XRP, Zcash, and TRON.
XRP, ETH, USDT, ZEC, USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX, TRX
This is the part users care about most. The crypto exchnage paused withdrawals as a safety step. It says this was not because user funds were at risk. Withdrawals will come back in stages. Big coins go first.
Timeline: Bitget Withdrawal Restoration Schedule
Sept 28, 8:00 UTC: BTC withdrawals return
Sept 29, 8:00 UTC: ETH withdrawals return (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism)
Sept 30, 8:00 UTC: USDT withdrawals return (Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Tron)
Oct 2, 8:00 UTC: Other coins, cash, and P2P return
These times equal 4:00 PM Beijing time on each date. The trading and deposits work fine right now.
Mandiant and SlowMist are still on the case. They work with Bitget's own team. The team has traced the stolen funds. They found the wallets the hackers used. This spans EVM chains, XRP Ledger , Zcash, and TRON. Police are also involved now.
The loss number could shift again. More checks may turn up more facts. But it still says the hack is contained. No new theft has occurred since.
It wants help getting the stolen funds back. So it made a bounty plan. Anyone can join: exchanges, security experts, or everyday sleuths. Here's how it works:
5% of any frozen funds go to the person who helped freeze them
5% of any recovered funds go to the person who helped recover them
The help must be voluntary, not court-ordered
The exchange picks who gets paid and how much
Bybit Lazarus Bounty tool will help run this effort
Stablecoin firms have also jumped in. CoinDesk reports that Circle and Tether froze one wallet tied to the crypto hack. That move locked up 218,023 USDT and 99,990 USDC. Together, that's about $318,000. Circle acted first, at 5:00 AM UTC on September 25. Tether followed soon after. MistTrack confirmed both moves.
This is a small piece of the total loss. MistTrack says other hacker wallets still hold over 63,000 ETH. Stablecoin firms can't freeze ETH the same way.
Binance founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao publicly responded to the Bitget hack, calling it a tough day for the exchange. He said he expects Binance, the BNB Chain ecosystem, and the wider crypto community to help out however they can. CZ also reminded users to put safety first during the incident, closing his post with Binance's familiar "Stay SAFU" message.
Other exchange leaders echoed similar support. Bybit CEO Ben Zhou, Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng, MEXC CEO Vugar Usi, and CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta all publicly offered assistance the same day, signaling a broader industry response to the hack beyond Bitget's own team.
You don't need to do anything before withdrawals return
Watch the Bitget app for withdrawal updates
Bitget Wallet is separate and was not affected by this hack
The crypto exchange fixed the bug from its September 24 hack. It will bring back withdrawals starting September 28. The loss estimate now stands near $387.5 million, mostly due to newly found Zcash and TRON funds.
Mandiant and SlowMist keep helping with the probe. Bitget's bounty plan and the Circle/Tether freeze mark early wins in getting funds back. Full recovery is still not certain.
YMYL Disclaimer: This article is for informational purposes only and is not financial advice. Crypto security incidents can change quickly. Readers should verify withdrawal status and new updates through Bitget's official channels before taking any action.

sources.text:
Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, ​a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. | REUTERS REUTERS SHARE/SAVE X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link Oct 30, 2026 Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial.
“This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance said in a ​post on X.

sources.title: How Chainalysis Used AI to Trace the $387M Bitget Theft
sources.text:
Crime How AI Helped Chainalysis Investigators Trace the $387 Million North Korea Stole from Bitget October 1, 2026 | Chainalysis Team Summary Since $387 million was stolen from Bitget on September 24, Chainalysis investigators have been working with the exchange and law enforcement partners to trace the stolen funds across multiple blockchains and protocols.
Our team quickly built custom tooling and automation for the investigation using our in-house AI. This helped investigators reduce tracing time, connect seemingly fragmented on-chain activity, and uncover new links across the investigation.
The DPRK-attributed attack pushes the total value of crypto stolen by North Korea actors in 2026 past $1 billion. In the coming weeks, our team will continue to monitor the stolen funds, label linked addresses, and share intelligence with counterparts.
When Chainalysis began tracing the $387 million stolen from Bitget last week, we knew the actors behind the exploit would move quickly. So our investigators leveraged in-house AI to create custom automations that matched their speed.
In a round-the-clock war room, our Customer Outcomes team kept Bitget and law enforcement partners updated with the latest insights Chainalysis derived while following the money. We boosted our efforts by building custom automation tools to move fast, cutting out manual tracing of complex transactions across multiple blockchains and reconciling activity at each step. We estimate that more than 20 hours of manual bridge reconciliation was compressed to under 10 minutes.
As can be seen in the graph below, which shows a portion of the transfers, hundreds of transfers have been carried out since the attack began. The funds were transferred between different networks, such as from Ethereum to Bitcoin.
Scaling cross-chain analysis with custom tooling
This wasn’t simply an AI-assisted tool to help our investigators build graphs. Our agentic platform gives our experts the ability to interrogate Chainalysis and other data sources to quickly develop custom solutions tailored to the specific investigation.
Importantly, this did not replace our investigative expertise. Rather, it accelerated it. Our investigators still defined the logic, reviewed the outputs, and directed the investigation.
The ability to quickly identify and understand illicit activity is increasingly important as DPRK and other threat actors use sophisticated automation to move and obscure stolen funds. Investigators must keep pace with these tactics while applying the judgment and expertise needed to make sense of complex on-chain activity.
That makes speed a critical part of the investigative process. Within minutes of identification, labels flagging stolen funds were live in our data platform, giving compliance teams and law enforcement the data they needed to act.
In the first three hours after the exploit, $387 million left Bitget across 23 transfers, landing on four chains: Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%), as shown below. From there, we identified distinct laundering mechanisms used by the threat actors, from cross-chain liquidity and messaging protocols to instant swaps. We also identified links to laundering services.
Our investigators’ ability to reconstruct the movements of funds across pathways using the custom tooling was particularly important for the stolen XRP. Rather than sending the XRP to an exchange, the attackers pushed it through a cross-chain liquidity protocol and took Bitcoin out the other side.
In simple terms, such protocols let someone deposit one asset on one chain and receive a different asset on another without an account or intermediary connecting the two sides. But each swap still leaves an on-chain record.
Our investigators matched deposits to their corresponding payouts, bridging the gap between blockchains and extending the trail.

sources.text:
Crime Treasury Sanctions Russians, North Koreans supporting DPRK IT Worker Fraud October 28, 2026 | Chainalysis Team Summary OFAC sanctioned Russian and DPRK nationals that targeted U.S. businesses with fraudulent IT workers, generating cryptocurrency proceeds to fund the North Korean regime and its weapons programs.
Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas converted millions of dollars in cryptocurrency on behalf of IT agencies that facilitated the placement of DPRK IT workers at target companies under false pretenses, enabling them to earn income.
DPRK nationals Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong managed groups of IT workers based in Russia, monitoring their work at victim companies and collecting the cryptocurrency income they generated.
On October 28, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes that generate hundreds of millions in revenue for DPRK’s weapons programs.
The action is the latest strike against a sprawling network of state sponsored North Korean agents who secretly seek employment in legitimate businesses, earn income, and pass that income along to fund the North Korean regime. This network has been growing in scope for years , posing a greater risk to corporations duped into hiring the agents, as well as providing Pyongyang with a steady flow of cash. In this instance, the DPRK workers and their facilitators leveraged Russian nationals to convert the crypto into cash.
North Korean IT worker operations now span dozens of countries and generate an estimated $250 to $600 million in annual revenue for the DPRK regime, according to the United Nations panel of Experts . The threat has drawn a coordinated response from U.S. authorities: In May 2022, the FBI, State Department, and Treasury issued a joint advisory detailing how DPRK IT workers use VPNs, stolen identities, and proxy infrastructure to pass themselves off as non-North Korean freelancers or applicants.
Since then, the U.S. Department of Justice has brought indictments against U.S.-based facilitators who operated laptop farms, forwarding equipment that helped DPRK IT workers fake a domestic presence during their employment at American companies. Today’s OFAC action targets the financial side of that same pipeline, the individuals and entities that convert the workers’ crypto earnings into usable funds for Pyongyang.
The latest action targets a handful of individuals who helped that network convert their crypto into cash. Russians Vitold Viktorovich Obertas and Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov converted millions of dollars for front companies that provided a cover for DPRK IT workers, including Alis and Amnokang, both of which have been previously sanctioned. Our research into the Russians finds their relationships to these illicit networks stretches back years.
The action also targets two DPRK nationals, Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong, who directly managed DPRK IT workers based in Russia. Both report to an umbrella company called Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company that OFAC designated in 2023 for its role in DPRK IT worker schemes. Our past research examines how groups like Chinyong launder crypto for the regime.

Since early 2025, Obertas has converted $2 million worth of cryptocurrency for DPRK officials, according to OFAC. But our research into his on-chain activity finds the relationship stretches back to early 2023.

sources.title: Bitget Loses USD 351.6 Million in Hot Wallet Breach in Likely North Korea Attack | TRM Labs
sources.text:
Bitget Loses USD 351.6 Million in Hot Wallet Breach in Likely North Korea Attack | TRM Labs Insights September 25, 2026 Bitget Loses USD 351.6 Million in Hot Wallet Breach in Likely North Korea Attack TRM Team On September 24, 2026, attackers moved an estimated USD 351.6 million out of Bitget’s hot and warm wallets across Ethereum, the XRP Ledger, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, BNB Chain, and Base. Bitget detected the unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC, paused withdrawals, and said the loss falls within its User Protection Fund. It is the largest crypto theft of 2026 by value so far. Key takeaways Attackers moved an estimated USD 351.6 million from Bitget’s hot and warm wallets on September 24, 2026. Bitget says they compromised a backend system, manipulated the transaction data shown to its authorization process, and caused it to approve the transfers. The exchange says its private keys were not stolen.
Early estimates of USD 170–190 million covered the EVM chains. TRM data shows about USD 158 million also left through the XRP Ledger, bringing the observed outflows close to Bitget’s reported loss.
The stolen ETH and XRP were quickly split among new wallets, many holding round amounts of roughly 10,000 ETH or 20 million XRP. By the morning of September 25, most of those funds had not moved again.
Bitget paused withdrawals and says its USD 464 million User Protection Fund covers the loss. It says cold wallets were unaffected.
Bitget’s CEO has described North Korean involvement as “very likely,” though TRM has not definitively attributed the attack. Multiple on-chain links to previously identified North Korean thefts, including Bybit and AFX Bridge, point toward North Korean involvement. Those links run through a laundering network TRM has not observed working with any other group, though another actor carrying out the theft remains technically possible.
Exchanges use hot and warm wallets to process withdrawals while keeping most customer assets in cold storage. Transfers from those wallets still require approval before they are signed. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said an attacker gained access to a backend system connected to its wallet infrastructure, spoofed transaction data, and triggered that approval process. Bitget says its private keys were not compromised and its cold wallets were unaffected.
The failure resembles the February 2025 Bybit theft in one respect: the attacker manipulated what the people or systems authorizing a transfer saw. At Bybit, that led signers to approve a transfer from a cold wallet. At Bitget, according to the exchange, it caused its withdrawal controls to authorize transfers from hot and warm wallets. Neither account depends on stolen private keys.
Early onchain estimates put the loss at USD 170–190 million because they covered Ethereum and other EVM chains. Bitget reported a loss of USD 351.6 million. TRM data shows approximately USD 158 million in XRP and USD 7 million in TRX also leaving Bitget wallets, bringing the observed outflows close to the exchange’s figure.
The proceeds were split into round-number wallets within hours
On Ethereum, much of the stolen value passed through 0x770b10b273fC44Fe9197D6bF20F145c2e98463Ee, which also received funds on Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, and Optimism. A second wallet, 0xa6dd3f218b65e32ccc37be30f74884133c655545, distributed its balance to newly created wallets over roughly two hours on the evening of September 24. Most received about 10,000 ETH each. Together with wallets funded directly from the first address, eight wallets received most of the stolen ETH. None had sent funds onward as of the morning of September 25.
The XRP followed a similar pattern. Funds leaving Bitget passed through smaller relay accounts before arriving in separate accounts holding round amounts of 20 million XRP. Most of that XRP also remained in place as of the morning of September 25.

OFAC Designates Facilitators of North Korean IT Worker Schemes Targeting US Businesses | TRM Labs Insights October 28, 2026 OFAC Designates Facilitators of North Korean IT Worker Schemes Targeting US Businesses TRM Team Key takeaways On October 28, 2026, OFAC designated ten individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korea IT worker schemes, targeting facilitators and workers based in North Korea and Russia.
OFAC says the schemes defraud US businesses and generate revenue for North Korea’s weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs.
Three of the designated individuals have cryptocurrency ties. The designation lists eight addresses for them, and TRM has added all of them to TRM under sanctions.
The action extends earlier designations of Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company (May 2023) and Amnokgang Technology Development Company (March 2026), and shows these networks relying on Russia-based delegations and intermediaries.
The newly designated First Financial and Technical Development Center, and six workers tied to it, generated more than USD 750,000 since 2025. The designation lists no crypto addresses for them.
On October 28, 2026, the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated ten individuals and one entity for their roles in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes. According to OFAC, these schemes defraud US businesses and generate revenue for North Korea’s weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. The designations target facilitators and North Korea IT workers based in North Korea and Russia, and build on OFAC's March 12, 2026 designation of a separate North Korea IT worker network.
Three of the designated individuals have cryptocurrency ties, and the designation lists eight cryptocurrency addresses for them. TRM Labs has added all three individuals and their addresses to TRM under sanctions.
A Russian intermediary for North Korean financial transactions
According to OFAC, Vitold Viktorovich Obertas is a Russian intermediary for illicit North Korean financial transactions, including for Amnokgang Technology Development Company, which OFAC designated on March 12, 2026. Since January 2025, Obertas has conducted nearly USD 2 million in cryptocurrency conversions and at least USD 1.25 million in other currency transactions for North Korean officials. OFAC designated Obertas under Executive Order (E.O.) 13687.
The Alis delegation and its facilitators
OFAC also targeted a Russia-based delegation of IT workers. Limited Liability Company Alis (Alis) is a Vladivostok-based company that the UN Panel of Experts flagged in March 2024 as a possible North Korean-Russian joint venture owned in part by a North Korean national. OFAC describes Alis as a subordinate of Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company (Chinyong), which OFAC designated in May 2023. According to OFAC, Kim Ki Hyok leads Alis's Russia-based delegation of North Korean IT workers and monitors the workers, ensures they meet their financial targets, and has transferred nearly USD 500,000 in cryptocurrency for the delegation since 2024. Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov has supported Alis since 2024 by exchanging and converting an equivalent of USD 3.5 million in cryptocurrency, monitoring cryptocurrency transactions, and providing logistical support. OFAC also designated Kim Hyo Dong, who leads a separate Russia-based Chinyong-subordinate delegation and has facilitated the transfer of over USD 100,000 equivalent in financial assets since at least December 2023. OFAC designated Kim Ki Hyok, Kim Hyo Dong, and Boykov under E.O. 13687.
The UN Panel of Experts has reported that Chinyong, which is subordinate to North Korea’s Ministry of People's Armed Forces, handled tens of millions of dollars in transactions between 2017 and 2022, using bank accounts in China and Russia to launder IT worker revenue. sources.title: Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) | North Korean IT Workers Expanding Use of Facilitators, Broadening Recruitment
sources.text:
Skip to main The Democratic People's Republic of Korea ( North Korea ) continues to improve its tactics to infiltrate western companies with thousands of state-controlled remote "IT Workers" ( ITW s) while avoiding detection. ITWs are increasingly using facilitators to counter improved private sector detections and law enforcement actions. The FBI has observed North Korean ITWs use stolen identities, extort victims, and use threats of physical violence to demand payments. ITWs fund North Korea's government, including its nuclear weapons and other military programs, and pose a significant national security and intellectual property theft insider threat. The FBI is updating its previous guidance to the public and private sector on techniques and recommendations to identify and avoid this threat. This includes tips to protect yourself and your business, as well as a larger description of how the threat has recently evolved. The general public needs to be aware that North Korean ITWs increasingly rely on the help of witting and unwitting Americans to acquire jobs in the United States, and they strategically target those under financial stress. ITWs are paying Americans for an expanding range of services to hide their own involvement in the scheme, including asking some to appear on camera, participate in job interviews or meetings, verify fraudulent identities, provide access to personal social media or professional networking accounts, ship packages, complete urinalysis tests or fingerprint submissions, or keep employment-related devices connected to the Internet from personal residences. These actions are illegal, and participating in them puts individuals at risk of law enforcement scrutiny. U.S. companies should recognize the scale, persistence, and rapid evolution of the North Korean ITW threat means ITWs cannot be identified reliably with a single indicator. Mirroring cybersecurity concepts, detection requires an "identity in depth" approach for effective defense, consisting of multiple layered access controls and detections throughout the employment lifecycle to find, interdict, and remove ITWs regardless of North Korean tactical innovations. Tips to Protect Yourself as an Individual For the public , the FBI provides the following information and general recommendations to prevent falling victim to the North Korean ITW scheme. Be aware North Korean ITWs post fake job openings on well-known job boards often as freelance gigs with simple requests such as interviewing on someone's behalf or receiving and hosting laptops in your home.
ITWs routinely invent elaborate stories, create fake companies, and produce official documentation to lend credibility to their requests. Common ITW backstories include claiming to be Chinese or East Asian nationals in need of a temporary U.S. presence or claiming to be Eastern Europeans displaced by the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
Reject any request to provide personal information, personal details, financial information, or personal account logins in exchange for payment.
Be aware ITWs have used threats of violence and other acts of intimidation to try to compel Americans to continue illicit activities. If you or someone you know receives a threat to life or is concerned about physical safety, call 911.
Tips to Protect Your Business — Identity in Depth
For companies , the FBI notes North Korean ITWs cannot be identified reliably with a single indicator or detection given the diversity of their activity and significant signature overlaps with legitimate remote employment. Finding ITWs in applicant pipelines or on corporate networks requires examining multiple compounding behaviors that may be innocuous individually, but when considered together are highly suggestive of malicious activity. Listed below are ITW behavioral tendencies and general recommendations.
ITWs continue to use remote desktop software to connect to employment-related devices. Examples include AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk

sources.title: Largest bank heist in history: Binance hack rocks crypto industry | Euronews
sources.text: Advertisement By&nbsp Angela Barnes Published on 30 October 2026 - 6:05 GMT+1 • Updated 8:20 Share Comments Add Euronews on Google Share Facebook Twitter Flipboard Send Reddit Linkedin Messenger Telegram VK Bluesky Threads Whatsapp Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around $6.3 billion (€5.5bn) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft. The company - the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes - posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, insisting that "user funds are completely safe" but also saying it would "cover all losses". ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Binance later said on its X account for Latin America that "the total estimated impact is around $6.3bn (€5.5bn)". "We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze the affected assets, with ~ $3bn (€2.6bn) frozen on-chain so far," it added. That would be more than four times the amount involved in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: $1.5bn (€1.3bn) taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform. The Bybit heist was attributed at the time to a group of hackers affiliated with North Korea called TraderTraitor. Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said on Thursday it had "high confidence" that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing "robust on and off-chain intelligence". "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists," TRM said. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group - which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for "The Interview", a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Fund freeze At about 0030 GMT (0230 CEST) on Friday, Binance said all deposits and withdrawals had been "temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement". "This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," the company said. The company's statement on X said an initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a "DevOps engineer", allowing the unauthorised party to access a "service container" and execute unauthorised withdrawal transactions. "We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets," Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete. Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether - a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT - said his firm had frozen about $1.6bn (€1.4bn) "related to a potential Binance exchange hack". Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than $800m (€696m) in USDC. USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins", or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Crypto prices tumble For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, with the exception of stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins. At about 0400 GMT (0600 CEST), bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6%, respectively. BNB, Binance's native cryptocurrency, was up 2.7% after tumbling nearly 10%. The attack on Binance comes as many observers express concerns that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. sources.text: Binance hit by $6.3 billion security breach in potential record crypto heist - France 24 Skip to main content Advertising Binance hit by $6.3 billion security breach in potential record crypto heist Binance said on Thursday that a security breach had affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially making it the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record. The world's largest crypto exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, while the incident sent Bitcoin and other digital currencies lower. Issued on: 30/10/2026 - 04:48 Modified: 30/10/2026 - 07:47 4 min Reading time Share By: FRANCE 24 (FILE) The logo of Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, which reported a crypto heist on October 29, 2026. © Justin Sullivan, AFP Binance , the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets . Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses". An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said. Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday. Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko. sources.title: North Korea Steals USD 6.36 Billion From Binance in the Largest Hack in History | TRM Labs
sources.text:
North Korea Steals USD 6.36 Billion From Binance in the Largest Hack in History | TRM Labs Insights October 29, 2026 North Korea Steals USD 6.36 Billion From Binance in the Largest Hack in History TRM Team Key takeaways On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC. That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025. Binance has confirmed a security incident and suspended withdrawals on several networks.
TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence. We make this judgment with high confidence. TRM is tracking the funds and alerting partners through the Beacon Network.
On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 pre-signed authorizations prepared in advance. In the same window, Binance wallets on the other nine chains sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's assessment, this points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure.
Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial froze about USD 2.67 billion in stablecoins, and Arbitrum's Security Council froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB on its network, for a total of roughly USD 2.7 billion. The attacker raced the freezes by selling USDT to market makers and borrowing ETH against USDT on Aave. It now holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about USD 2.4 billion in assets beyond any issuer's reach.
On the evening of October 29, billions of dollars in crypto began leaving wallets belonging to Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Within minutes, Binance wallets on the XRP Ledger, Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and four other networks had sent their balances to addresses controlled by a single attacker. A second wave around 23:05 UTC reached Binance wallets on Avalanche and Polygon.
Binance said it was investigating a potential security issue, then said it had temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks as a precaution. Binance has said user funds are safe. The story is still developing, and the figures here reflect what TRM saw onchain as of October 30 at 00:30 UTC.
TRM attributes this attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s premier hacking unit. We base this assessment on robust on and off-chain intelligence sources. The FBI named the same group as responsible for the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst. The laundering observed so far, built on large swaps through market makers and lending protocols, differs from the bridge-heavy pattern that followed Bybit. TRM will share further findings as the investigation develops.
TRM traced every transfer from Binance-attributed wallets to attacker-controlled addresses across ten blockchains. Valuing each transfer at the price of the asset at the moment it was taken, the total is approximately USD 6.36 billion. At current prices, the same assets are worth about USD 6.23 billion.
Ethereum accounts for about USD 3.79 billion. That includes 200,630 ETH and 185 other tokens, among them 1.875 billion USDT, 823 million USDC and 88.5 million RLUSD. Bitcoin outflows total 18,270 BTC, about USD 1.47 billion. Tron outflows total 612.7 million USDT and 46.4 million TRX, about USD 628 million. The XRP Ledger lost 233.46 million XRP, about USD 296 million. Solana outflows total 970,500 SOL, about USD 96 million. Arbitrum, Optimism and Base combine to about USD 39 million, including 74.6 million ARB taken on Arbit

sources.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by hack suspected to be largest in history - BBC News
sources.text:
Image source, Reuters By Osmond Chia , Business reporter and Angus Thompson Published 30 October 2026, 00:37 GMT
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".
The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach".
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens.
Western security agencies have previously said stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile development programs.
The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.
Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
"That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement.
"To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak."
He said a detailed "post-mortem" would be shared once the investigation was complete.
In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them."
Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform B
